schema_status.note: Task-scoped owner evidence manifest for a supervisor runtime repair. This is not a product-level loop manifest: the task changes orchestrator task-state read/verify logic, the supervisor reconciliation phase, and their regression suites, and claims no hosted activation, deployment, or capital authority.

task.title: Bound supervisor task-state lock latency and projection truth

scope.owned_layer: The authoritative task-state journal read/verify contract; supervisor runtime-admission boundaries for provider probes, GitHub bus network work, worker-base fetches, and termination polling; dispatch-status workspace lease propagation; and exact task-branch remote-tracking refresh.
scope.not_changing: No .orchestrator/config.json edit, no hand-edited ai-status.json / current-work.md / ai-activity-log.jsonl, no live worker signal or task-board mutation, no change to the event schema, hash chain, nonterminal-drop guard, dispatch ordering, provider routing, or product service code.

observed_failures.summary: Supervisor PID 901543 stamped a tick heartbeat at 22:35:04Z and completed it at 22:47:55Z (771s) while reviewer and status processes queued on runtime-admission inode 807896; the task-state reviewer reopen waited about nine minutes. A further exclusive hold ran from at least 22:50:27Z to 22:59:04Z (~517s), and Codex2 BFF reopen PID 480495 waited from about 22:51:17Z and committed only at 22:59:45Z.
observed_failures.root_cause: Replay cost inside the canonical lock. sync_task_state_shadow replayed and revalidated the entire journal four times per cycle (load_events, project_latest_state, then verify_projection loading and projecting it again), and common.load_status replayed it twice on each of its many per-cycle calls. validate_event canonically re-serializes each event's full state twice, so cost scaled with journal size on every pass.
observed_failures.fixed_by: load_snapshot / verify_snapshot: one lock window, one validated pass, with a validated-prefix checkpoint and an mmap-ed read.

observed_failures.summary: Lock-free Human/Ops note commands over the ~157MB / 2050-event journal each required roughly 55-90s.
observed_failures.root_cause: One governed status command replayed the journal four times: load_events plus project_latest_state to read the board, then append_state_commit loading the whole journal for the head and replaying it a second time purely to read back the line it had just appended.
observed_failures.fixed_by: load_snapshot for the read; an offset-and-size readback of exactly the appended bytes for the commit.

observed_failures.summary: caught_up was inverted. A healthy cycle published caught_up=false; a cycle that had just rewritten a drifted board published caught_up=true.
observed_failures.root_cause: caught_up was assigned the divergence predicate (sha(file) != sha(journal) in authoritative mode, not before['ok'] in shadow mode) and then reused as the phase's changed signal, so one field carried two contradictory meanings.
observed_failures.fixed_by: caught_up is now parity after reconciliation (report['ok']); a separate repaired flag records whether a write was needed, and repaired is what the phase returns as its changed signal.

observed_failures.summary: A verifier begun around the 22:48 lock handoff transiently reported event_count=2046 with the expected SHA from event 2045 and the projected SHA from event 2046 while a concurrent append landed; a stable rerun at event 2049 then returned ok=true.
observed_failures.root_cause: Two lock domains. scripts/verify_task_state_store.py read ai-status.json with no lock and then called verify_projection, which opened its own shared store-lock window; a commit landing between the two reads produced a report whose count came from one journal generation and whose compared digest came from another.
observed_failures.fixed_by: verify_snapshot is pure and derives every field from one snapshot; the verifier samples the board and the journal inside one canonical task-state lock domain.

observed_failures.summary: The provider capability probe, which shells out to gh for auth and version checks, ran inside the exclusive runtime-admission hold.
observed_failures.root_cause: load_provider_report was called from _run_once_locked, which executes entirely inside runtime_state_lock(shared=False).
observed_failures.fixed_by: probe_provider_reports runs in run_once before the lock is acquired and its result is passed into the locked cycle.

observed_failures.summary: A 771s exclusive hold left no trace in runtime state, so the stall was only discoverable from reviewer complaints and lock inode inspection.
observed_failures.root_cause: Cycle duration was stamped, but the exclusive-hold duration -- the actual ceiling on every worker status command's wait -- was never published.
observed_failures.fixed_by: record_runtime_lock_hold publishes runtime_lock_hold_seconds, runtime_lock_hold_peak_seconds, and runtime_lock_hold_exceeded each cycle, warning past supervisor.runtime_lock_hold_warn_after_seconds (default 30s).

observed_failures.summary: Four live worker dispatches between 12:35Z and 14:42Z failed their immediate status sync because ORCH_RUN_ID was set while PANTHEON_WORKTREE_ROOT and ORCH_WORKSPACE_PATH were unset.
observed_failures.root_cause: sync_dispatched_task_status propagated only the worker run id. The status lease validator correctly rejected an incomplete identity even though the Claude/Codex adapter process itself had both workspace variables.
observed_failures.fixed_by: Both process_queue call sites and the deferred sync tuple carry the exact resolved worker workspace. status_command_subprocess_context clears inherited lease variables, then binds both workspace names. A run id without a workspace is refused before subprocess launch.

observed_failures.summary: A worker with a master-only remote.origin.fetch ran git fetch origin dev, but origin/dev remained stale while the remote dev tip had advanced.
observed_failures.root_cause: An explicit branch name updates FETCH_HEAD; it does not guarantee the remote-tracking destination is updated when the configured fetch refspec excludes that branch.
observed_failures.fixed_by: Supervisor prefetch and task Git helpers use +refs/heads/<base>:refs/remotes/origin/<base>. The network fetch runs before runtime admission, and the locked phase fails closed unless that exact base was refreshed.

integrity_rules.every_byte_is_hashed_on_every_read: The checkpoint records a SHA-256 over the exact byte prefix it summarizes. A read recomputes that hash over the journal on disk and rejects the checkpoint on any mismatch, so an edited, reordered, or truncated prefix always falls back to a full replay and is caught by the chain validator.
integrity_rules.what_the_checkpoint_actually_saves: Only the per-event canonical re-serialization and digest work for events whose bytes are unchanged. Validation is a pure function of those bytes, so an unchanged prefix means the earlier verdict still holds.
integrity_rules.checkpoint_is_never_the_authority: Missing, unreadable, wrong-version, wrong-schema, symlinked, self-inconsistent, or prefix-head-mismatched checkpoints all degrade silently to a full replay. The recorded head must equal the actual last JSONL event in the claimed byte prefix and is re-validated before use.
integrity_rules.deep_audit_escape_hatch: PANTHEON_TASK_STATE_STORE_FULL_REPLAY=1, or verify_task_state_store.py --full-replay, re-parses and revalidates every event and refuses to read or write the checkpoint.
integrity_rules.mmap_safety: The journal is mapped read-only inside the store lock. Readers hold it shared and writers exclusively, so the mapped range cannot be rewritten or truncated while it is in use.
integrity_rules.append_durability: append_state_commit fsyncs the file and its directory, then confirms the file's size equals the pre-append size plus the payload and that the payload bytes are present at their offset. A short or partial write raises 'task-state append readback mismatch' instead of being accepted.

acceptance.statement: Supervisor never holds runtime-admission, task-state, or event-log exclusive locks across provider probes, network subprocess waits, or poll sleeps.
acceptance.delivered: Provider probes, GitHub bus network work, and exact worker-base fetches run before runtime admission. Worker confirm/kill polling runs after lock release, with one pre-sent SIGTERM and Linux start-tick binding to prevent PID-reuse signalling. Journal work remains one snapshot pass, and every cycle publishes the measured exclusive hold.

acceptance.statement: Task-state authoritative reconciliation validates one stable journal snapshot without duplicate full replay under the canonical lock.
Concurrent approve, assign, note, and reviewer commands complete within two seconds p95 during active supervisor cycles over a 2000-event / 134MB fixture.
acceptance.measured: Refreshed on the second-pass branch: 2050-event / 159.5MB fixture, 4 concurrent commands against a continuously cycling supervisor: p50 1.114s, p95 1.179s, max 1.179s. Legacy shape on the same fixture: p50 59.737s, p95 63.463s.

acceptance.statement: caught_up is true whenever projection equals canonical state after reconciliation, and a separate repaired flag records whether a write was needed.
Concurrent append and reconciliation preserve monotonic sequence, exact projection SHA, queue leases, and no lost state.
acceptance.detail: Sequence and previous-hash chaining are unchanged and still enforced by validate_event on every appended event and replayed tail. A report is built from one snapshot, so a commit landing mid-phase cannot split it across generations. Dispatch sync now carries the existing queue lease's exact run id and workspace; it does not create or replace queue leases.

acceptance.statement: Regression reproduces the live PID 901543 multi-minute lock wait and proves reviewer approve no longer stalls.
acceptance.detail: task_state_lock_latency_bench.py builds a 2050-event / 159.5MB journal and runs reviewer-approve-shaped commands against a supervisor that is actively cycling under the real canonical task-state lock. The refreshed legacy shape reproduces the live 55-90s command cost at 59.737s p50 / 63.463s p95; the second-pass branch returns 1.179s p95. The harness exits non-zero if current p95 crosses 2s.

acceptance.statement: No config edit, manual worker termination, or task-board mutation; branch, PR checks, review, merge, and evidence complete.
acceptance.detail: Implementation and owner validation are complete with no .orchestrator/config.json change, no live process signalled, and no generated status file hand-edit. PR checks, independent Codex2 review, merge, and owner closeout remain pending at this evidence revision.

negative_tests.required_case: tampered history behind a valid checkpoint
negative_tests.asserts: Rewriting one event in the middle of a checkpointed journal breaks the prefix hash, forces a full replay, and raises TaskStateStoreError. The checkpoint cannot launder an edited event.

negative_tests.required_case: truncated journal behind a stale checkpoint
negative_tests.asserts: A checkpoint claiming more bytes than the file holds is refused; the snapshot reflects the events that actually survive.
A garbage checkpoint degrades to a full replay rather than raising, and the healthy read repairs the cache instead of leaving it poisoned.

negative_tests.required_case: checkpointed result must equal a full audit
negative_tests.asserts: event_count, last_event_id, state, and state_sha256 are identical between the accelerated read and PANTHEON_TASK_STATE_STORE_FULL_REPLAY=1.

negative_tests.required_case: partial write must not be accepted as committed
negative_tests.asserts: A write that reports success while landing only part of the payload raises 'task-state append readback mismatch'; the O(1) readback is not weaker than the full replay it replaces.

negative_tests.required_case: empty authoritative journal must not fall back to the board
negative_tests.asserts: An empty journal is reported as an error and ai-status.json is left untouched.

negative_tests.required_case: corrupt journal must not touch canonical state
negative_tests.asserts: The phase degrades, records last_error, and leaves ai-status.json byte-identical.

negative_tests.required_case: nonterminal drop guard still applies on the new append path
negative_tests.asserts: validate_state_transition is still called with the previous state taken from the snapshot head, so OPS-TASK-STATE-NONTERMINAL-DROP-GUARD-001 is unchanged in effect.
With write_json stubbed out, the authoritative branch re-reads the board, finds it still divergent, raises, and publishes ok=false / caught_up=false instead of claiming parity.

negative_tests.required_case: dispatch run id without exact workspace binding
negative_tests.asserts: The supervisor refuses the dispatch status sync before spawning ai_status.py; inherited lease variables are cleared and cannot substitute for the worker's exact workspace.

negative_tests.required_case: master-only remote fetch refspec leaves origin/dev stale
negative_tests.asserts: The fixture proves plain git fetch origin dev advances FETCH_HEAD but not origin/dev, then proves the explicit source:destination refspec advances origin/dev to the exact remote commit.
The post-lock confirmer compares process start ticks and treats the original worker as gone when the numeric PID now belongs to another process, without sending another signal.

non_interference.hash_chain: unchanged; sequence and previous_event_sha256 are still validated for every event on every full replay and for every tail event on every accelerated read
non_interference.nonterminal_drop_guard: unchanged; still invoked from append_state_commit with the previous state read from the journal head
non_interference.public_api: load_events, project_latest_state, append_state_commit, and verify_projection keep their signatures and behaviour; load_snapshot and verify_snapshot are additions
non_interference.worker_termination: no live worker was signalled; code changes defer bounded confirmation outside runtime admission and prevent duplicate/PID-reuse signals
non_interference.generated_mirrors: dashboard-bundle.json and docs-site/dashboard-bundle.json were dirtied by the test suites and restored before staging

commands.command: PYTHONPATH=.orchestrator python3 -m pytest -q .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py .orchestrator/test_runtime_state.py .orchestrator/rewrite/test_task_state_store.py .orchestrator/rewrite/test_worker_lifecycle.py .orchestrator/test_common.py scripts/test_ai_status.py scripts/test_verify_task_state_store.py scripts/test_status_file_guard.py

commands.conclusion: meets_target true. Uncontended p95 14.844s legacy -> 0.263s current (56.4x). Under an active supervisor cycle p95 63.463s legacy -> 1.179s current (53.8x). Cold first read with no checkpoint 3.281s once.

cold_read_after_journal_replacement.description: The first read after the checkpoint is absent or invalidated pays a full replay: 3.281s on the 159.5MB fixture, against about 0.25s for a checkpointed read.
cold_read_after_journal_replacement.containment: It is a one-time cost per journal generation, paid by whichever caller reads first, and it is strictly cheaper than the four full replays every caller paid before. It is bounded by journal size, not by concurrency.
cold_read_after_journal_replacement.recheck_trigger: If task-state commands regress to multi-second latency, check whether <journal>.checkpoint.json is being repeatedly invalidated -- that would indicate something is rewriting journal history rather than appending to it.

checkpoint_shares_the_journal_trust_doma.description: The checkpoint binds a validated head to an exact byte prefix by SHA-256, so an edited journal is always caught. An actor able to write both the journal and a matching checkpoint could in principle present a self-consistent forgery.
checkpoint_shares_the_journal_trust_doma.containment: That actor can already rewrite the journal itself. The checkpoint lives in the same directory, is created 0600, is replaced atomically, and is never trusted without recomputing the prefix hash. verify_task_state_store.py --full-replay ignores it entirely for audits.
checkpoint_shares_the_journal_trust_doma.recheck_trigger: Any change to who may write the runtime directory holding the event log.

contention_scales_with_concurrent_writer.description: Governed status commands take the canonical task-state lock exclusively, so latency grows with the number of simultaneous commands. Refreshed p95 at 4 concurrent commands plus an active supervisor is 1.179s against a 2s target.
contention_scales_with_concurrent_writer.containment: Per-command cost on the 159.5MB fixture is ~0.263s, so the target holds with headroom at the concurrency the live system exhibits (the incident involved two waiting reopens).
contention_scales_with_concurrent_writer.recheck_trigger: If routine concurrency rises well above four simultaneous status commands, or if the journal grows several times beyond 160MB, re-run the bench and consider journal compaction.
